title: Saag Aloo
subtitle: Spiced potato and spinach curry
excerpt: Cubed potatoes cooked with onion, garlic, ginger, and warm spices, then combined with wilted spinach. A simple, deeply satisfying vegetarian curry that pairs with almost anything.

recipe.sourceNotes: Saag aloo is a Punjabi dish of spinach (saag) and potato (aloo) that became one of the most popular vegetarian curries in British Indian restaurants from the 1970s onwards. Saag can refer to any leafy green in Punjabi cooking, but in the restaurant context it almost always means spinach. The dish is a dry or semi-dry curry rather than a sauce-based one: the spinach is added near the end and should wilt into the spiced potato rather than creating a soupy liquid.

content.text: Par-boil the potatoes first so they finish cooking in the spice base without taking too long. The spinach is added at the very end and only wilted: too much heat drives off the moisture and turns it grey. Fresh or frozen spinach both work; frozen should be defrosted and squeezed dry before adding.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes

content.text: Par-boil the potato cubes in salted boiling water for 8 minutes until just starting to soften. Drain.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes.

Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli powder. Cook for 1 minute. Add the par-boiled potato. Stir to coat in the spices. Add 100 ml of water. Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potato is fully tender.
Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring until wilted. Add the garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Serve with rice or naan.
